notes:
What's new

- HTML now renders in the real browser engine (WebView2) with page scripting switched off, so layouts, tables, images and CSS match the web. If WebView2 is not installed, the built-in reader view still opens the page.
- WebP and JPEG XL now decode with their own bundled decoders, so they work on a clean Windows install without Store extensions. Ctrl+C on a web page copies its text.
- A signing self-test tool proves the release signing path end to end with a temporary certificate.
- Public CI now also builds and checks the bundled WebP/JPEG XL decoders and the HTML paths.
changelog: WinPreview 1.3.29 - bundled codecs + browser HTML, with a headless CI gate. bundled codecs + browser HTML. Vendored libwebp 1.5.0 (decoder subset, C/SSE2) and the official libjxl 0.13.0 Windows runtime with app-local VC++ runtime; WebP/JXL no longer depend on Store codecs. Added a WebView2 HTML view (scripts/dialogs/web messages/devtools/context menus/host objects disabled) with reader fallback, Esc forwarding, Ctrl+C page text, and a page-only --html-capture test hook. tests/html_view_test.py covers rendering, script safety and fallback (14 checks). tools/sign-selftest.ps1 exercises the signing pipeline with a temporary self-signed cert. CI matrix now includes WebP and JXL fixtures. CI now verifies every generated fixture through --screenshot plus a new --diagnostics JSON (docType, sheets/slides/chapters, codec pages), so the matrix runs without an interactive desktop.
